result.instructions: Tools for AddEvent, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which events do I have scheduled next month?"; "List all the calendars in my account with their titles."; "Who has RSVP'd so far to my open house event, and what did they answer?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes AddEvent data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run addevent_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run addevent_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run addevent_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. addevent_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: addevent_list_calendars
tools.title: List calendars
tools.description: List the account's calendars (newest first by default) with id, title, timezone, whether it is the default calendar, landing-page links and counts of events and subscribers. GET /calendars.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

tools.name: addevent_get_calendar
tools.title: Get calendar
tools.description: One calendar by id: title, timezone, week start, template ids, subscriber and event counts, links, custom data. GET /calendars/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_create_calendar
tools.title: Create calendar
tools.description: WRITE: creates a new calendar in the AddEvent account (a new, empty calendar; nothing existing is changed and nobody is notified). Needs a title. POST /calendars.

timezone.description: Default timezone for events on this calendar (IANA name).

description.description: Shown on the calendar landing page.

landing_page_template_id.description: Calendar landing page template id, or 'default' (see addevent_list_calendar_templates).

custom_data.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs to store on the object (snake_case keys), e.g. an external id.

tools.name: addevent_update_calendar
tools.title: Update calendar
tools.description: WRITE: changes fields of an existing calendar (only the fields you pass; the rest stay). Title, description and timezone changes show on its landing page and can reach people who subscribe to the calendar feed. Not reversible by this server (no previous values are kept), so read the calendar first. PATCH /calendars/{id}.

timezone.description: IANA timezone such as America/Los_Angeles, or 'floating' (same local time for everyone). See addevent_list_timezones.

custom_data.description: Key-value pairs to store on the calendar (snake_case keys).

tools.name: addevent_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: Search the account's events (newest created first; by start time when a date filter is used): title, start/end, timezone, location, RSVP settings and stats, landing-page links. Filter by calendar, event ids, text, date window or a custom_data pair. GET /events.

calendar_ids.description: Only events on these calendar ids.

starts_before.description: Only events that start before this date-time (datetime_max; naive comparison, timezones ignored).

ends_after.description: Only events that end after this date-time (datetime_min; naive comparison, timezones ignored).

search.description: Case-insensitive text in title, internal name, description or location.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

tools.name: addevent_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event by id (evt-...): all fields incl. description, organizer, reminder, recurring rule, RSVP settings and stats, custom data and share links. GET /events/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_create_event
tools.title: Create event
tools.description: WRITE: creates a new event on a calendar (the account's default calendar if calendar_id is omitted). Creates a public event landing page and share links; it does not e-mail anyone, though people subscribed to that calendar's feed will see the event on their next sync. Needs title and datetime_start. POST /events.

datetime_start.description: Start date-time: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm or YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.

calendar_id.description: Calendar to add the event to (see addevent_list_calendars); default calendar if omitted.

datetime_end.description: End date-time (default: start + 1 hour). Same formats as the start.

all_day_event.description: All-day event: only the dates are used.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the start/end (default: the calendar's timezone), or 'floating'.

recurring_rule.description: iCalendar recurrence rule such as FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10. The start must match the rule. Omit for a one-off event; on update an empty string makes the event stop repeating.

description.description: Plain text or simple HTML (keep under ~500 characters for cross-browser links).

location.description: Address or URL (meeting link). Use either location or location_id, not both.

location_id.description: Id of a saved location (0 = none). Not together with location.

reminder.description: Minutes before the start for a calendar-app reminder (0-10800).

free_busy.description: How the event shows in an attendee's calendar.

landing_page_template_id.description: Event landing page template id or 'default' (see addevent_list_event_templates).

rsvp_enabled.description: Require an RSVP before the event can be added to a calendar.

custom_data.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs to store on the object (snake_case keys), e.g. an external id.

tools.name: addevent_update_event
tools.title: Update event
tools.description: WRITE: changes fields of an existing event (only the fields you pass; the rest stay). The change goes live on its landing page and share links, and people who subscribed to the calendar or added the event with a live link are updated on their next calendar sync, so a time or location change can notify real people. No previous values are kept: read the event first. PATCH /events/{id}.

datetime_start.description: New start: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm or YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.

calendar_id.description: Move the event to this calendar id.

datetime_end.description: End date-time (default: start + 1 hour). Same formats as the start.

all_day_event.description: All-day event: only the dates are used.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the start/end (default: the calendar's timezone), or 'floating'.

recurring_rule.description: iCalendar recurrence rule such as FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10. The start must match the rule. Omit for a one-off event; on update an empty string makes the event stop repeating.

description.description: Plain text or simple HTML (keep under ~500 characters for cross-browser links).

location.description: Address or URL (meeting link). Use either location or location_id, not both.

location_id.description: Id of a saved location (0 = none). Not together with location.

reminder.description: Minutes before the start for a calendar-app reminder (0-10800).

free_busy.description: How the event shows in an attendee's calendar.

landing_page_template_id.description: Event landing page template id or 'default' (see addevent_list_event_templates).

rsvp_enabled.description: Require an RSVP before the event can be added to a calendar.

custom_data.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs to store on the object (snake_case keys), e.g. an external id.

tools.name: addevent_list_rsvp_attendees
tools.title: List RSVP attendees
tools.description: List RSVP attendees (personal data: e-mail addresses and the answers they gave on the RSVP form). Filter by calendar, event or response (going/maybe/not-going). Paged, 20 at most per page: read only what the task needs. IP address and coordinates are removed from the reply. GET /rsvps.

event_ids.description: Only attendees of these event ids.

calendar_ids.description: Only attendees of events on these calendar ids.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

tools.name: addevent_get_rsvp_attendee
tools.title: Get RSVP attendee
tools.description: One RSVP attendee by id (personal data: e-mail and form answers; IP address and coordinates removed). GET /rsvps/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_create_rsvp_attendee
tools.title: Create RSVP attendee
tools.description: WRITE: adds ONE RSVP attendee (one e-mail address, personal data) to an event. This server never asks AddEvent to send the confirmation or organizer notification e-mails, but the event's own reminder and follow-up e-mails (if the event has them) will later go to this address, so only add someone who really RSVP'd. The e-mail must be unique per event. POST /events/{id}/rsvps.

rsvp_form_data.description: Answers to the event's RSVP form as field-name -> value. The default form needs {"name": "..."}.

tools.name: addevent_update_rsvp_attendee
tools.title: Update RSVP attendee
tools.description: WRITE: changes ONE RSVP attendee (email, response or form answers; only the fields you pass). The event's reminder and update e-mails go to the e-mail address stored here, so changing it redirects those e-mails to that person. This server never triggers the confirmation or organizer notification e-mails. PATCH /rsvps/{id}.

rsvp_form_data.description: Answers to the event's RSVP form as field-name -> value. The default form needs {"name": "..."}.

tools.name: addevent_list_calendar_subscribers
tools.title: List calendar subscribers
tools.description: List people subscribed to the account's calendars (personal data: the form answers they gave, such as name and e-mail; calendar app type, sync status). Paged, 20 at most per page. IP address and coordinates are removed. GET /subscribers.

calendar_ids.description: Only subscribers of these calendar ids.

status.description: active = synced in the last 30 days; inactive = not; blocked = blocked by the owner. AddEvent returns only active ones when omitted, so call once per status.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

tools.name: addevent_get_calendar_subscriber
tools.title: Get calendar subscriber
tools.description: One calendar subscriber by id (personal data; IP address and coordinates removed). GET /subscribers/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_list_rsvp_forms
tools.title: List RSVP forms
tools.description: The account's RSVP forms (id, name), newest first. Use the id as rsvp_form_id on an event. GET /events/rsvp-forms.

tools.name: addevent_list_event_templates
tools.title: List event landing page templates
tools.description: The account's event landing page templates (id, name), newest first. Use the id as landing_page_template_id on an event. GET /events/templates.

tools.name: addevent_list_calendar_templates
tools.title: List calendar templates
tools.description: The account's calendar landing page templates or embeddable calendar templates (id, name), newest first. Use the id as landing_page_template_id / embeddable_calendar_template_id on a calendar. GET /calendars/templates.

tools.name: addevent_list_timezones
tools.title: List timezones
tools.description: Timezone names AddEvent supports (use them as the timezone of events and calendars), with current UTC offset. Optional text filter on the name. GET /timezones.

search.description: Case-insensitive part of the name, e.g. 'Prague' or 'America/'.
